title: Boss: Nothing gets through
summary: Parse a config file safely, validate an insurance claim, and price a basket with pattern-matched rules, without one unplanned crash.

steps.title: The brief
body: Five pieces of code that sit on the edge of a system, where the input is whatever the outside world felt like sending. The last one goes straight into your Sidekick.
1. Read one line of a settings file with the Try pattern.
2. Look settings up and convert them, returning a `Result` that says why when it cannot.
3. Validate an insurance claim: collect every error, and throw a custom exception that carries them.
4. Price items with pattern matching, turning expected failures into results and letting real bugs through.
5. Score your own tasks, so `sk` shows the most important ones first.
Where a stage uses it, this type is **provided for you**, exactly as in the last lesson:
The tests check the exact error messages, so copy them carefully.

steps.title: Stage 1: One line of config
prompt: A settings file has lines such as `port = 8080`. Write
`bool TryParseSetting(string line, out string key, out string value)`
- a valid line is `key=value`. Split at the **first** `=`, and trim spaces from both parts.
- return `false` when the line is empty or only spaces, starts with `#` (a comment), has no `=`, or has nothing before the `=`
- an empty value is fine: `"name="` gives key `"name"` and value `""`
- whenever you return `false`, set both `key` and `value` to `""`
```csharp
TryParseSetting(" port = 8080 ", out var k, out var v);   // true: "port", "8080"
TryParseSetting("url=http://x?a=1", out k, out v);        // true: "url", "http://x?a=1"
TryParseSetting("# a comment", out k, out v);             // false

> **Tip:** `line.IndexOf('=')` gives the position of the first `=`, or `-1` if there is none. `line.Substring(0, i)` is the text before position `i`, and `line.Substring(i + 1)` is everything after it.
starter: bool TryParseSetting(string line, out string key, out string value)
// return false for blank lines, comments, and lines with no usable key
solution: bool TryParseSetting(string line, out string key, out string value)
template: {{CODE}}
string dojoK, dojoV;
Dojo.Eq("\"port=8080\" returns true", true, TryParseSetting("port=8080", out dojoK, out dojoV));
Dojo.Eq("...key is port", "port", dojoK);
Dojo.Eq("...value is 8080", "8080", dojoV);
Dojo.Eq("\" host = example.com \" returns true", true, TryParseSetting(" host = example.com ", out dojoK, out dojoV));
Dojo.Eq("...key is trimmed to host", "host", dojoK);
Dojo.Eq("...value is trimmed to example.com", "example.com", dojoV);
Dojo.Eq("\"url=http://x?a=1\" returns true", true, TryParseSetting("url=http://x?a=1", out dojoK, out dojoV));
Dojo.Eq("...the value keeps its own = sign", "http://x?a=1", dojoV);
Dojo.Eq("\"name=\" returns true", true, TryParseSetting("name=", out dojoK, out dojoV));
Dojo.Eq("...with an empty value", "", dojoV);
Dojo.Eq("an empty line returns false", false, TryParseSetting("", out dojoK, out dojoV));
Dojo.Eq("a line of spaces returns false", false, TryParseSetting("    ", out dojoK, out dojoV));
Dojo.Eq("\"# port=1\" is a comment: false", false, TryParseSetting("# port=1", out dojoK, out dojoV));
Dojo.Eq("...and key is reset to empty", "", dojoK);
Dojo.Eq("\"just text\" has no =: false", false, TryParseSetting("just text", out dojoK, out dojoV));
Dojo.Eq("\" = 5\" has no key: false", false, TryParseSetting(" = 5", out dojoK, out dojoV));
Dojo.Eq("...and value is reset to empty", "", dojoV);
hints: Trim the line first and work with the trimmed copy. Two quick exits: it is `""`, or it `StartsWith("#")`.
Find the first `=` with `IndexOf('=')`. If that is `-1`, return `false`.
Take `Substring(0, at).Trim()` as the key. If it is empty, return `false` **before** assigning `key`, so both outputs stay `""`. Otherwise set `key` and `value` and return `true`.

steps.title: Stage 2: Settings you can trust
prompt: The lines are now in a `Dictionary<string, string>`. Write three methods to read from it safely. `Result<T>` is provided.
**`string? Find(Dictionary<string, string> config, string key)`**: the value, or `null` when the key is missing
**`string GetOrDefault(Dictionary<string, string> config, string key, string fallback)`**: the value, or `fallback` when the key is missing
**`Result<int> GetInt(Dictionary<string, string> config, string key, int min, int max)`**
- key missing: fail with `"Missing setting: port"`
- not a whole number: fail with `"port must be a whole number"`
- outside `min` to `max`: fail with `"port must be between 1 and 65535"`
- otherwise succeed with the number
(Those messages are for the key `"port"` with a range of 1 to 65535. Build them from the arguments.)
starter: string? Find(Dictionary<string, string> config, string key)
string GetOrDefault(Dictionary<string, string> config, string key, string fallback)
Result<int> GetInt(Dictionary<string, string> config, string key, int min, int max)
solution: string? Find(Dictionary<string, string> config, string key)
if (config.TryGetValue(key, out string? value)) return value;
string GetOrDefault(Dictionary<string, string> config, string key, string fallback)
Result<int> GetInt(Dictionary<string, string> config, string key, int min, int max)
return Result<int>.Fail($"{key} must be a whole number");
return Result<int>.Fail($"{key} must be between {min} and {max}");
template: {{CODE}}
var dojoCfg = new Dictionary<string, string> { ["port"] = "8080", ["host"] = "example.com", ["retries"] = "lots", ["timeout"] = "0" };
Dojo.Eq<string?>("Find returns the value for a known key", "example.com", Find(dojoCfg, "host"));
Dojo.Eq<string?>("Find returns null for a missing key", null, Find(dojoCfg, "colour"));
Dojo.Eq("GetOrDefault returns the value for a known key", "example.com", GetOrDefault(dojoCfg, "host", "localhost"));
Dojo.Eq("GetOrDefault returns the fallback for a missing key", "blue", GetOrDefault(dojoCfg, "colour", "blue"));
Dojo.Eq("GetInt(port, 1, 65535) succeeds", true, GetInt(dojoCfg, "port", 1, 65535).IsSuccess);
Dojo.Eq("...with the value 8080", 8080, GetInt(dojoCfg, "port", 1, 65535).Value);
Dojo.Eq("a missing key fails", false, GetInt(dojoCfg, "workers", 1, 8).IsSuccess);
Dojo.Eq("...with: Missing setting: workers", "Missing setting: workers", GetInt(dojoCfg, "workers", 1, 8).Error);
Dojo.Eq("text that is not a number fails with: retries must be a whole number", "retries must be a whole number", GetInt(dojoCfg, "retries", 0, 5).Error);
Dojo.Eq("a number below min fails with: timeout must be between 1 and 60", "timeout must be between 1 and 60", GetInt(dojoCfg, "timeout", 1, 60).Error);
Dojo.Eq("a number above max fails with: port must be between 1 and 1024", "port must be between 1 and 1024", GetInt(dojoCfg, "port", 1, 1024).Error);
Dojo.Eq("min and max themselves are allowed", true, GetInt(dojoCfg, "timeout", 0, 60).IsSuccess && GetInt(dojoCfg, "port", 1, 8080).IsSuccess);
class Result<T>
public bool IsSuccess { get; }
public T? Value { get; }
public string Error { get; }
private Result(bool isSuccess, T? value, string error) { IsSuccess = isSuccess; Value = value; Error = error; }
public static Result<T> Ok(T value) => new Result<T>(true, value, "");
public static Result<T> Fail(string error) => new Result<T>(false, default, error);
hints: `Find` is the `ContainsKey` pattern again: return `config[key]` if it is there, otherwise `null`. `GetOrDefault` is then one line with `??`.
`GetInt` is three guard clauses in a row, each returning `Result<int>.Fail(...)`: is `Find(config, key)` null, does `int.TryParse` fail, is the number outside the range?
Build the messages with interpolation: `$"Missing setting: {key}"`, `$"{key} must be a whole number"`, `$"{key} must be between {min} and {max}"`.

steps.title: Stage 3: A claim validator
prompt: Claims arrive from a web form with fields missing. Write three types.
**`Claim`**: a record with `PolicyNumber` (`string?`), `Amount` (`decimal`), `Description` (`string?`), in that order
**`InvalidClaimException : Exception`**
- constructor `InvalidClaimException(List<string> errors)`
- property `Errors` (`IReadOnlyList<string>`, `get` only)
- `Message` is the errors joined with `"; "`
**`ClaimValidator`** (a static class)
`static List<string> Validate(Claim? claim)` returns every problem, in this order:
- a `null` claim: just `"Claim is missing"`, and nothing else
- `"Policy number is required"` when it is null, empty or only spaces
- `"Amount must be positive"` when it is 0 or less
- `"Amount is over the 50000 limit"` when it is more than 50000
- `"Description must be at least 10 characters"` when it is null or shorter than that
`static void EnsureValid(Claim? claim)` does nothing for a valid claim, and throws `InvalidClaimException` carrying the errors for an invalid one.
Aim for zero warnings and no `!`.
starter: record Claim(string? PolicyNumber, decimal Amount, string? Description);
solution: record Claim(string? PolicyNumber, decimal Amount, string? Description);
errors.Add("Description must be at least 10 characters");
template: var dojoGood = new Claim("P-204", 1200m, "Burst pipe in the kitchen");
Dojo.Eq("a complete claim has no errors", new List<string>(), ClaimValidator.Validate(dojoGood));
Dojo.Eq("a null claim gives exactly: Claim is missing", new List<string> { "Claim is missing" }, ClaimValidator.Validate(null));
Dojo.Eq("a null policy number is reported", new List<string> { "Policy number is required" }, ClaimValidator.Validate(dojoGood with { PolicyNumber = null }));
Dojo.Eq("a policy number of spaces is reported", new List<string> { "Policy number is required" }, ClaimValidator.Validate(dojoGood with { PolicyNumber = "   " }));
Dojo.Eq("an amount of 0 is reported", new List<string> { "Amount must be positive" }, ClaimValidator.Validate(dojoGood with { Amount = 0m }));
Dojo.Eq("an amount of 50000.01 is reported", new List<string> { "Amount is over the 50000 limit" }, ClaimValidator.Validate(dojoGood with { Amount = 50000.01m }));
Dojo.Eq("an amount of exactly 50000 is fine", new List<string>(), ClaimValidator.Validate(dojoGood with { Amount = 50000m }));
Dojo.Eq("a null description is reported", new List<string> { "Description must be at least 10 characters" }, ClaimValidator.Validate(dojoGood with { Description = null }));
Dojo.Eq("a 9-character description is reported", new List<string> { "Description must be at least 10 characters" }, ClaimValidator.Validate(dojoGood with { Description = "Wet floor" }));
Dojo.Eq("a 10-character description is fine", new List<string>(), ClaimValidator.Validate(dojoGood with { Description = "Wet floors" }));
var dojoBad = new Claim(null, -5m, null);

Dojo.Eq("three problems give three errors, in order", new List<string> { "Policy number is required", "Amount must be positive", "Description must be at least 10 characters" }, ClaimValidator.Validate(dojoBad));
Dojo.Check("InvalidClaimException inherits from Exception", typeof(Exception).IsAssignableFrom(typeof(InvalidClaimException)), "class InvalidClaimException : Exception");
var dojoEx = new InvalidClaimException(new List<string> { "A", "B" });
Dojo.Eq("the exception's Message joins the errors with \"; \"", "A; B", dojoEx.Message);
Dojo.Eq("the exception's Errors holds the list", 2, dojoEx.Errors.Count);
Dojo.Try("EnsureValid does nothing for a valid claim", () => { ClaimValidator.EnsureValid(dojoGood); Dojo.Check("EnsureValid does nothing for a valid claim", true); });
Dojo.Throws<InvalidClaimException>("EnsureValid throws InvalidClaimException for a bad claim", () => ClaimValidator.EnsureValid(dojoBad));
Dojo.Throws<InvalidClaimException>("EnsureValid throws InvalidClaimException for null", () => ClaimValidator.EnsureValid(null));
int dojoCount = -1;
try { ClaimValidator.EnsureValid(dojoBad); } catch (InvalidClaimException dojoCaught) { dojoCount = dojoCaught.Errors.Count; } catch (Exception) { }
Dojo.Eq("...and the thrown exception carries all 3 errors", 3, dojoCount);
{{CODE}}
hints: Handle `claim is null` first and return straight away. After that check, the compiler knows `claim` is safe to use.
The two amount rules cannot both be true, so `if ... else if` is fine there. For the description, `claim.Description?.Length ?? 0` gives 0 when it is missing.
The exception: `public InvalidClaimException(List<string> errors) : base(string.Join("; ", errors)) { Errors = errors; }`. `EnsureValid` calls `Validate` and throws only when `errors.Count > 0`.

steps.title: Stage 4: Pricing rules
prompt: Last stage: a pricing engine. These types **already exist** for you, along with `Result<T>`:
```csharp
record Book(decimal Price);
record Food(decimal Price, bool Perishable);
record GiftCard(decimal Value);
class PricingException : Exception   // new PricingException("message")
**`decimal UnitPrice(object? item)`**: one switch expression, first match wins
- a `Book` priced over 20: 10% off, so `Price * 0.9m`
- any other `Book`: its `Price`
- a perishable `Food`: half price
- any other `Food`: its `Price`
- a `GiftCard`: its `Value`
- `null`: throw `ArgumentNullException`. That is a bug in the caller.
- anything else: throw `new PricingException("No pricing rule for this item")`
**`Result<decimal> Quote(object? item, int quantity)`**: the safe front door
- `quantity` of 0 or less: fail with `"Quantity must be positive"`
- `item` is null: fail with `"Item is required"`
- `UnitPrice` throws `PricingException`: catch **only that** and fail with its `Message`
- otherwise succeed with unit price times quantity
> **Tip:** `throw` can be the result of a switch arm: `null => throw new ArgumentNullException("item"),`
starter: // Book, Food, GiftCard, PricingException and Result<T> are provided.
solution: _ => throw new PricingException("No pricing rule for this item")
template: {{CODE}}
Dojo.Try("a 30 book gets 10% off: 27", () => Dojo.Eq("a 30 book gets 10% off: 27", 27m, UnitPrice(new Book(30m))));
Dojo.Try("a book of exactly 20 is full price", () => Dojo.Eq("a book of exactly 20 is full price", 20m, UnitPrice(new Book(20m))));
Dojo.Try("perishable food at 8 is half price: 4", () => Dojo.Eq("perishable food at 8 is half price: 4", 4m, UnitPrice(new Food(8m, true))));
Dojo.Try("other food at 8 is 8", () => Dojo.Eq("other food at 8 is 8", 8m, UnitPrice(new Food(8m, false))));
Dojo.Try("a 25 gift card is 25", () => Dojo.Eq("a 25 gift card is 25", 25m, UnitPrice(new GiftCard(25m))));
Dojo.Throws<ArgumentNullException>("UnitPrice(null) throws ArgumentNullException", () => UnitPrice(null));
Dojo.Throws<PricingException>("UnitPrice(\"a string\") throws PricingException", () => UnitPrice("a string"));
Dojo.Try("Quote(book at 30, 2) succeeds with 54", () => { var dojoR = Quote(new Book(30m), 2); Dojo.Eq("Quote(book at 30, 2) succeeds with 54", 54m, dojoR.IsSuccess ? dojoR.Value : -1m); });

Dojo.Try("Quote(perishable food at 3, 5) succeeds with 7.5", () => { var dojoR = Quote(new Food(3m, true), 5); Dojo.Eq("Quote(perishable food at 3, 5) succeeds with 7.5", 7.5m, dojoR.IsSuccess ? dojoR.Value : -1m); });

Dojo.Try("quantity 0 fails with: Quantity must be positive", () => { var dojoR = Quote(new Book(5m), 0); Dojo.Eq("quantity 0 fails with: Quantity must be positive", "Quantity must be positive", dojoR.IsSuccess ? "(succeeded)" : dojoR.Error); });

Dojo.Try("a null item fails with: Item is required", () => { var dojoR = Quote(null, 1); Dojo.Eq("a null item fails with: Item is required", "Item is required", dojoR.IsSuccess ? "(succeeded)" : dojoR.Error); });

Dojo.Try("a bad quantity is reported before a missing item", () => { var dojoR = Quote(null, -1); Dojo.Eq("a bad quantity is reported before a missing item", "Quantity must be positive", dojoR.IsSuccess ? "(succeeded)" : dojoR.Error); });

Dojo.Try("an unknown item fails with the PricingException's message", () => { var dojoR = Quote(42, 1); Dojo.Eq("an unknown item fails with the PricingException's message", "No pricing rule for this item", dojoR.IsSuccess ? "(succeeded)" : dojoR.Error); });
record Book(decimal Price);
record Food(decimal Price, bool Perishable);
record GiftCard(decimal Value);
class PricingException : Exception
public PricingException(string message) : base(message) { }
class Result<T>
public bool IsSuccess { get; }
public T? Value { get; }
public string Error { get; }
private Result(bool isSuccess, T? value, string error) { IsSuccess = isSuccess; Value = value; Error = error; }
public static Result<T> Ok(T value) => new Result<T>(true, value, "");
public static Result<T> Fail(string error) => new Result<T>(false, default, error);
hints: A type pattern and a property pattern combine, and you can still name the result: `Book { Price: > 20 } b => b.Price * 0.9m,`. It must come before the plain `Book b` rule.
The last two arms throw instead of returning a value: `null => throw new ArgumentNullException("item"),` then `_ => throw new PricingException("No pricing rule for this item")`.

`Quote` has two guard clauses that return `Result<decimal>.Fail(...)`, then a `try` that returns `Result<decimal>.Ok(UnitPrice(item) * quantity)` and a `catch (PricingException ex)` that returns `Result<decimal>.Fail(ex.Message)`.

steps.title: Stage 5: Sidekick's priority rules
prompt: Last stage, and it goes straight into your Sidekick: the rules that decide what `sk` shows under **Next up**.
Your `TaskItem` (with `Tag`, `Due` and `EstimateMinutes`) is ready.
**`static int PriorityScore(TaskItem task, DateOnly today)`**
- a finished task scores `0`, whatever else is true.
- otherwise start at `10`, then add (use `switch` expressions with relational patterns):
- due date, by days left (`due.DayNumber - today.DayNumber`): overdue `+50`, today `+40`, 1-2 days `+25`,
3-7 days `+10`, later `+0`; no due date `+0`.
- tag: `urgent +30`, `bug +20`, `blocked -15`, `chore -5`, anything else or none `+0`.
- a quick task (estimate 1 to 30 minutes) `+5`; a running timer `+15`.
**`static List<TaskItem> TopPriorities(IEnumerable<TaskItem> tasks, DateOnly today, int count)`**
The open tasks, highest score first, ties by lower `Id`, at most `count` of them.
```text
today = Wed 25 Nov 2026
"Fix login" tag bug, due today, est 45      -> 10 + 40 + 20      = 70
"Upgrade" tag chore, no due date, est 120    -> 10 - 5            = 5
"Typo" est 10, due Fri 27 Nov               -> 10 + 25 + 5       = 40
starter: static int PriorityScore(TaskItem task, DateOnly today)
static List<TaskItem> TopPriorities(IEnumerable<TaskItem> tasks, DateOnly today, int count)
solution: static int PriorityScore(TaskItem task, DateOnly today)
static List<TaskItem> TopPriorities(IEnumerable<TaskItem> tasks, DateOnly today, int count)
return open.Count <= count ? open : open.GetRange(0, count);
hints: `if (task.Due is DateOnly due) { int days = due.DayNumber - today.DayNumber; score += days switch { < 0 => 50, 0 => 40, <= 2 => 25, <= 7 => 10, _ => 0 }; }`
`task.Tag switch { "urgent" => 30, ... , _ => 0 }` also handles a null tag in the `_` arm.
`open.Sort((a, b) => ...)`: compare scores the other way round (`b` before `a`) for highest first, then `a.Id.CompareTo(b.Id)`.
template: {{CODE}}
var dojoToday = new DateOnly(2026, 11, 25);
TaskItem DojoTask(int id, string title, int est = 0, string? tag = null, int? dueIn = null)
var t = new TaskItem(id, title, est) { Tag = tag };
if (dueIn is int d) t.Due = dojoToday.AddDays(d);
return t;
var dojoLogin = DojoTask(1, "Fix login", 45, "bug", 0);
var dojoUpgrade = DojoTask(2, "Upgrade", 120, "chore");
var dojoTypo = DojoTask(3, "Typo", 10, null, 2);
Dojo.Eq("bug, due today, 45 min = 70", 70, PriorityScore(dojoLogin, dojoToday));
Dojo.Eq("chore, no due date = 5", 5, PriorityScore(dojoUpgrade, dojoToday));
Dojo.Eq("quick, due in 2 days = 40", 40, PriorityScore(dojoTypo, dojoToday));
Dojo.Eq("overdue = 60", 60, PriorityScore(DojoTask(4, "Late", 0, null, -1), dojoToday));
Dojo.Eq("due in 5 days = 20", 20, PriorityScore(DojoTask(5, "Soon", 0, null, 5), dojoToday));
Dojo.Eq("due in 30 days = 10", 10, PriorityScore(DojoTask(6, "Later", 0, null, 30), dojoToday));
Dojo.Eq("urgent = 40", 40, PriorityScore(DojoTask(7, "Now", 0, "urgent"), dojoToday));
Dojo.Eq("blocked = -5", -5, PriorityScore(DojoTask(8, "Wait", 0, "blocked"), dojoToday));
var dojoRunning = DojoTask(9, "Running", 60);
dojoRunning.Start(new DateTime(2026, 11, 25, 9, 0, 0));
Dojo.Eq("a running timer adds 15", 25, PriorityScore(dojoRunning, dojoToday));
var dojoDone = DojoTask(10, "Done", 20, "urgent", 0);
dojoDone.Complete();
Dojo.Eq("a finished task scores 0", 0, PriorityScore(dojoDone, dojoToday));
var dojoAll = new List<TaskItem> { dojoUpgrade, dojoTypo, dojoDone, dojoLogin, DojoTask(11, "Also 40", 0, "urgent") };
Dojo.Eq("TopPriorities: highest first, ties by id, done left out", new List<int> { 1, 3, 11 }, TopPriorities(dojoAll, dojoToday, 3).Select(t => t.Id).ToList());
Dojo.Eq("TopPriorities with a large count lists every open task", 4, TopPriorities(dojoAll, dojoToday, 10).Count);
Dojo.Eq("TopPriorities of nothing is empty", 0, TopPriorities(new List<TaskItem>(), dojoToday, 3).Count);
class TaskItem
string? tag;
public TaskItem(int id, string title, int estimateMinutes = 0)
if (id < 1) throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(nameof(id), "Task ids start at 1.");
if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(title)) throw new ArgumentException("A task needs a title.", nameof(title));
if (estimateMinutes < 0) throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(nameof(estimateMinutes), "An estimate cannot be negative.");
Id = id;
Title = title.Trim();
EstimateMinutes = estimateMinutes;
public int Id { get; }
public string Title { get; }
public int EstimateMinutes { get; }
public int LoggedMinutes { get; private set; }
public bool IsRunning { get; private set; }
public DateTime StartedAt { get; private set; }
public bool Done { get; private set; }
public string? Tag
get => tag;
set => tag = string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(value) ? null : value.Trim().ToLowerInvariant();
public string? Project { get; set; }
public DateOnly? Due { get; set; }
public string Label()
string tagPart = Tag is null ? "" : $" [{Tag}]";
string projectPart = Project is { Length: > 0 } p ? $" @{p}" : "";
string duePart = Due is DateOnly d ? $" (due {d:ddd d MMM})" : "";
return Title + tagPart + projectPart + duePart;
public void Start(DateTime at)
if (Done) throw new InvalidOperationException("A finished task cannot be started.");
if (IsRunning) return;
StartedAt = at;
IsRunning = true;
public int Stop(DateTime at)
if (!IsRunning) return 0;
if (at < StartedAt) throw new ArgumentException("A timer cannot stop before it started.", nameof(at));
int minutes = (int)(at - StartedAt).TotalMinutes;
LoggedMinutes += minutes;
IsRunning = false;
return minutes;
public void Log(int minutes)
if (minutes < 1) throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(nameof(minutes), "Log at least one minute.");
LoggedMinutes += minutes;
public void Complete()
IsRunning = false;
Done = true;
steps.explain: Each rule is one arm of a switch expression, so the policy reads like a table and changing a weight is a one-line edit. `sk` sorts your open tasks with exactly this score every morning.
